page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What species richness is
steps.why: Species richness is a count and nothing more, so the definition must say number of species and name the area it is counted in.
common_mistakes: Writing that species richness is the same as species diversity. Richness counts species only; diversity also takes in how many individuals each species has.
Leaving out the area. Richness is always a number per unit area.
steps.memory_tip: Rich means how many: species richness is a head count of species in a given area.
steps.margin_note: One sentence. Name the number and the unit area.
lines: Species richness is the number of species
The more species an area holds, the greater

steps.label: The species-area relation
steps.why: The relation between the number of species and the area plots as a straight line on a log scale, so the equation is that straight line written out, with Z as its slope.
common_mistakes: Writing the letters without saying what they stand for. Each symbol carries part of this mark.
Reading Z as the area. Z is the slope of the line; A is the area.
steps.memory_tip: S for species, A for area, Z for the slope of the line joining them.
steps.margin_note: The equation on its own line, then one short line for each letter.
lines: Species richness rises with the area studied.

lines.text: log S = log C + Z log A

lines: Z = slope of the line (regression coefficient)

insider_note: Write the species-area equation even though the question only says 'define' — the book's answer prints it, and the examiner expects every letter to be explained.
